🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Sold the US More Than Ever in August: $60.6 Billion</u>

Mexican exports to the United States hit $60.6 billion in August, the highest monthly figure on record and 34% more than a year earlier, El Financiero reports. January–August shipments reached $419.3 billion, up 18%, giving Mexico 17.4% of all US imports, ahead of Canada at 11.2% and Taiwan at 7.7%. Tariff threats and all, Mexico is still Washington's number-one supplier.
banner: US IMPORTS: MEXICO RECORD $60.6B IN AUGUST

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Morena Asks Electoral Authorities to Follow the Dollars Behind the Trending Topics</u>

Morena's Mexico City chapter asked the INE and the city's electoral institute to document every form of foreign intervention ahead of the 2027 elections. "There are truckloads of millions of dollars inflating trends on social networks, wanting to buy the public conversation," said state party leader Paulo García González. The request comes days after Bolivia arrested the prosecutor investigating Fernando Cerimedo, the Argentine operative whose network reaches Mexico's PRI.
banner: MORENA TO INE: TRACE FOREIGN DOLLARS

🇲🇽🩺 <u>73,000 Health Workers Sign Up for Mexico's New Neighborhood Clinics</u>

Since the call opened on September 14, 73,000 doctors, nurses and technicians have applied to staff Mexico's new Primary Health Care Clinics. The government is opening 12,750 of them across the 24 IMSS-Bienestar states starting in January 2027, each stocked with 60 basic medicines, internet and electronic medical records. They will treat patients whether or not they have social security.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Palestine Asks Mexico to Check Its Companies Profiting From the Occupation</u>

Palestine's ambassador to Mexico, Nadya Rasheed, asked the Senate to review the value chains of Mexican corporations tied to illegal Israeli settlements. Mexican conglomerate Orbia is among 61 firms just added to the UN human rights office's list of 214 companies doing business in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem. Mexico defends international law at every forum, she said, but "what has been lacking are consequences when that law is systematically violated."
banner: UN SETTLEMENT LIST NAMES MEXICO'S ORBIA

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Investment in Mexico Grows at Its Fastest Pace in Two Years</u>

Mexico's gross fixed investment grew 6.0% year on year in July, according to INEGI. That is the fastest pace since July 2024 and the fourth monthly gain in a row, after a 17-month losing streak. Private investment rose 5.9%, its best figure in 30 months, and public investment grew 6.9%. Construction spending was up 6.9% and machinery and equipment 4.9%, El Financiero reports.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Bolivia Arrests the Prosecutor Investigating Cerimedo</u>

Mexico's government links Argentine consultant Fernando Cerimedo to bot campaigns against the 4T. He has just lost the prosecutor on his case. On October 1, Bolivian authorities arrested Attorney General Roger Mariaca for illicit enrichment. Mariaca was personally handling the attempted-femicide case against Cerimedo. The arrest came two days after Cerimedo's ex-partner, Nadia Beller, posted photos of him with Donald Trump Jr., Brad Parscale and Dick Morris. Morris helped run Calderón's 2006 campaign, the one behind the "López Obrador, a danger to Mexico" attacks. Beller: "Everything points to a persecution so that Fernando Cerimedo goes free."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Took the Contract, Delivered Nothing: Supplier Fined 2.4 Million and Banned</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry has fined one supplier and two companies a combined 2.77 million pesos. Víctor Manuel Mercado Huerta won a direct contract from the state firm Exportadora de Sal and never delivered, installed or started up any of the equipment. He was fined 2.4 million pesos and banned for 37 months. A copper supplier to the Defense Ministry never signed its contract. A Health Ministry contractor submitted fake SAT, IMSS and Infonavit compliance certificates. All three are now barred from government contracts.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Parties Crying "Dictatorship" Have a Long Record of Massacres</u>

Mexico's PRI and PAN now call the 4T an authoritarian "dictatorship." A Contralínea piece by Aníbal García Fernández lists their own record in power: the Dirty War, Tlatelolco in 1968, the Halconazo, Acteal, Atenco, the APPO, Calderón's "war," Nochixtlán, Ayotzinapa and Ostula. "They are the ones who closed off dialogue and gave us bullets, repression, prison and human rights violations." He argues the dictatorship label is part of a "cultural battle" to erase that memory before 2027 and 2030.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro Hit Its 2026 Goal Early</u>

Mexico's youth apprenticeship program has closed sign-ups until the end of the year. That isn't because it ran out of steam. "It's not that the program is suspended, the goal was met," Sheinbaum said. The 2026 target was 500,000 young people, with a budget of 25.17 billion pesos. Labor Secretary Marath Bolaños says 619,000 apprentices have been served so far this administration, at a cost of 44 billion pesos. Registration reopens in January 2027.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>AMLO on Ambassador Johnson: "A Meddlesome Cop, Not a Diplomat"</u>

In his new book "Pueblo," former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador writes that US Ambassador Ronald Johnson "acts as an excited and meddlesome police officer" instead of a diplomat. When the CIA's illegal role in Chihuahua came out, he says, Johnson answered in a "defiant, non-diplomatic" tone and threatened to sue Mexican politicians in US courts. The book comes out the same week Sheinbaum told the Foreign Ministry to call Johnson in. He had broken ground on a police academy in Querétaro without telling the federal government.
banner: AMLO: US ENVOY IS A "MEDDLESOME COP"
